subject: Cumulus Health pilot: GPU shortlist, streaming behavior & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cumulushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-11T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Cumulus Health pilot: GPU shortlist, streaming behavior & pilot next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we draft the pilot statement of work. I focused this on the performance commitments you flagged and what we need from your side to size a Dedicated pool correctly.

Recap of perf targets you mentioned
- Production SLOs: p95 latency goal "for user-facing completions" ~ <= 300ms for 512-token responses (you said interactive chat with short context).
- Concurrent sessions: typical peak concurrent active users ~ 220–350; conservative planning target: 350 concurrent steady sessions.
- Streaming: you need partial-token streaming (word/phrase-level) for the UI as we render results incrementally. Baseline require the response stream to begin within 100ms of first token generation.
- Throughput: average qps now ~ 45 calls/sec with 1.8k tokens/call median; pilot expected to exercise higher token rates — please see attachment streaming_latency_samples.csv for current traces you sent.

Initial capacity options (shortlist) — tradeoffs we discussed
1) H100 (80GB) x2 nodes — best for low-latency larger-context workloads and parallel concurrency; higher absolute throughput, better KV-cache headroom for 4k+ context. Expected: 2xH100 pilot target to reach ~200–350 concurrent sessions for medium-length generations with p95 ~200–350ms depending on gen length and beam settings.
2) A100 (80GB) x3 nodes — more cost-effective at sustained throughput, slightly higher latency variance under bursty traffic, good fallback if H100 constraints occur.
3) L4 (48GB) x4 or L4+quantized config — lower-cost option for embedding/short-completion workloads; not ideal for 4k contexts or heavy streaming.

What we recommend for the pilot
- Pilot config: 2xH100 nodes, reserved throughput target 600k tokens/min (config set for 350 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled).
- SLO gating: p95 latency <= 350ms for 512 tokens; p99 <= 700ms. If pilot meets p95 consistently for 3 days under synthetic load + production-shadow, we can scale down the margin.
- Streaming behavior: enable early flush (partial token buffering = 32 tokens) to start letter/word streaming inside 100–150ms after generation begins. We'll tune prefix caching to keep p95 low for repeated prompts.

Data we need from you to finalize sizing and the SOW:
- Confirm expected 95th percentile prompt+response token lengths (median + 95th).
- Confirm production QPS and any daily/hourly seasonality windows.
- Procurement contact + PO timeline (we can start a pilot on a Temp Agreement while legal finalizes).

I've attached a pilot matrix (cumulus_pilot_matrix.xlsx) with a few knobs and a one-page mutual action plan (pilot_mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf). If we get the token profile and procurement contact, we can produce a firm, line-item pilot quote by EOD Friday.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm token profile and loop in procurement (Procurement@cumulushealth.com).
- Us: we’ll produce pilot SOW and a short test harness for the streaming validation (we’ll run a 48–72h soak with traffic shaped to peak concurrency).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cumulushealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cumulushealth.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@cumulushealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cumulus Health pilot: GPU shortlist, streaming behavior & pilot next steps

Priyom —

Appreciate the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 512-token p95 target is for UI latency (time-to-first-meaningful-chunk) rather than full-response completion. If you can guarantee the early flush behavior you describe, that works.
- Median token lengths are ~1.4k tokens (we often send longer clinical context), 95th ~3.1k. That will affect the H100 vs A100 decision — we'll push to provide a fuller distribution by EOD Thu.
- Peak concurrency can spike to ~480 for brief 15–20 minute windows during morning shift; sustained concurrency is closer to your 350 number.

We added procurement on the loop (Procurement). Procurement: can you confirm whether Redwood provides a short-term pilot invoice/PO path? We can sign a pilot MSA for up to 60 days.

Also tagging Maya — she'll own performance testing from our side. Maya, any questions on the metrics Priyom proposed?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Integrations, Cumulus Health
alex.rivera@cumulushealth.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cumulushealth.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@cumulushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-13T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cumulus Health pilot: GPU shortlist, streaming behavior & pilot next steps

Alex / Maya —

Thanks for the token distribution and spike info — that pushes us toward the H100 baseline for the pilot so we have cache headroom for 3k+ contexts. We’ll prepare two explicit costed options in the SOW:

A) H100 pilot (recommended): 2xH100, streaming enabled, reserved throughput cap 750k tokens/min, test harness to validate p95 early-flush latency <= 350ms for 512 tokens and time-to-first-chunk <= 150ms. Includes a 48h soak + 1h engineering sync per day during soak.
B) A100 alternative: 3xA100, reserved throughput 850k tokens/min, slightly higher cost-efficiency at steady-state but may require extra nodes for the same tail latency during morning spikes.

We’ll also include an L4/quantized option as a low-cost non-starter for the long-context use cases — documented purely for comparison.

Action items and timing
- Maya: if you can share the token distribution CSV and a sample of the UI streaming traces (just header + timestamps if needed) by EOD Thu, we’ll finalize the load-profile.
- Procurement: if you can confirm pilot PO cadence (Net 30 after pilot invoice vs upfront charge), we’ll put the right billing terms in the SOW.
- Redwood: Marissa and Ben — can you prep a short test harness (simple JMeter-based runner + streaming client) and the pricing rows for A vs H configs? Hoping to have the draft SOW by Friday.

Forwarding the pilot matrix and sample latency traces again — feel free to annotate.

On the legal/billing note — we can do a short-term pilot MSA (60 days) with a capped spend; procurement can pay upon invoice after the pilot if that’s standard. We’ll make the invoice explicit in the SOW so procurement can sign off quickly.

Cheers,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
